auditor_role: Principal Optimization and Operations Research Engineer

issues.description: Historical CP-SAT solver implementation included constant delay and turnaround buffer risk terms into the decision variable coefficients x[f, g]. Because each flight must be assigned to exactly one gate (sum_g x[f, g] == 1), adding an exogenous flight-level constant across all gates added large values to the integer scaling without changing the optimal decision, leading to integer scaling distortion.
issues.repair_description: CP-SAT decision model now optimizes strictly decision costs (reassignment + remote overflow stand penalty). Exogenous delay and turnaround risk costs are separated as reporting metrics and evaluated in the common evaluator evaluate_gate_assignment().

issues.description: Historical evaluation function directly accepted solver status strings (e.g. status='FEASIBLE') as proof of feasibility without independent outside constraint verification.
issues.repair_description: evaluate_gate_assignment() now delegates feasibility certification entirely to verify_hard_constraints_independently(). OptimizationResult.feasible is True if and only if all hard constraints pass and unassigned_count == 0.

issues.description: Historical evaluation tracked a single 'conflicts' counter that conflated planned hard constraint violations with realized post-hoc overlaps arising from stochastic operational arrival delays.
issues.repair_description: Separated into explicit machine-readable fields: hard_constraint_violations_count (planned violations), planned_conflict_count, and realized_post_hoc_conflicts_count (post-hoc conflicts under actual operational delays).

issues.description: Historical code occasionally treated overflow remote apron assignments and unassigned flights interchangeably, obscuring whether an assignment was a valid remote parking plan or a complete assignment failure.
issues.repair_description: Created explicit GateAssignmentState Enum (CONTACT_GATE, REMOTE_STAND, UNASSIGNED). Remote stands have infinite capacity and incur overflow penalty; unassigned flights are strictly infeasible and incur 2x overflow penalty.

issues.description: Simulated Annealing was historically treated as an equal peer to CP-SAT and benchmarked with unbounded or unequal runtime budgets, occasionally leading to unsupported claims of SA superiority.
issues.repair_description: Established strict solver hierarchy: DeterministicGreedy baseline, CP-SAT exact solver (budget T), and SA refinement (T/2 CP-SAT incumbent + T/2 SA refinement, total compute <= T). SA refinement can never be claimed as superior to an optimal CP-SAT.

issues.description: Historical documentation contained narrative claims implying 'real-world gate conflict reduction' or 'actual airport operational savings' despite BTS dataset having zero physical gate assignment ground truth.
issues.legacy_code_location: Historical V4 documents and summary logs
issues.repair_description: Instituted Hard V4 Claim Boundary: all downstream evaluation is defined strictly as synthetic gate assignments and simulated operational scenarios. All narrative claim strings updated across docstrings and manifests.
